# E0225: error raised by a macro

The macro rejected its input, and its message says why. Change the use to give it what it expects.

- Rule: [`macros.raised-errors`](../../reference/16-meta.md#macros.raised-errors)
- Reported at: the raised error's span, or the string literal that names the file it lies in.
- Tier: `meta`, checked in the `types` phase

## What the compiler prints

The program [`E0225_error_raised_by_a_macro`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0225_error_raised_by_a_macro):

`main.lt`:

```stilt fragment
meta use units

fn main() / io {
  let timeout = units.seconds!(90, sec)
  print("{timeout}")
}
```

```stilt fragment
use std.meta

/// The seconds in a duration of a number and a unit, `s`, `min` or `h`, as
/// `seconds!(90, min)`.
pub macro seconds(n: meta.Expr, unit: meta.Tokens) -> meta.Expr / raise<meta.Error> {
  var c = meta.cursor(unit)
  let name = try c.name()
  try c.end()
  let factor = match name.text() {
    "s" => 1,
    "min" => 60,
    "h" => 3600,
    other => raise meta.error(name.span(), "`{other}` isn't a unit: write `s`, `min` or `h`"),
  }
  quote { $n * $factor }
}
```

```stilt fragment
// The matchers of log lines: steps that move the threads of a match along a line, which the
// patterns of `patterns` compose. Each step takes the threads in the order the match prefers
// them, and gives the threads that come out of each in that order, the first at each position
// kept, so that a match is the one that backtracking would find, leftmost and greedy.

/// One way the match can stand: its position in the line, and the start and end of each group,
/// -1 while the group has taken no part.
pub type Thread = { at: i64, caps: List<i64> }

/// The characters of a line, and the threads of a match over them, in the order it prefers them.
pub type Run = { chars: List<str>, threads: List<Thread> }

/// What a match found: the text of each group, the whole match first, and `None` for a group
/// that took no part.
pub type Captures = { groups: List<Option<str>> }

impl Captures {
  /// The text of group `i`, or `""` when it took no part.
  /// ex: Captures { groups: [Some("ab"), None] }.get(1) == ""
  pub fn get(self, i: i64) -> str { self.groups[i] else "" }

  /// Whether group `i` took part in the match.
  /// ex: Captures { groups: [Some("ab"), None] }.has(0)
  pub fn has(self, i: i64) -> bool { self.groups[i].is_some() }

  /// The digits of group `i` as a number, or 0 when there are none.
  /// ex: Captures { groups: [Some("42")] }.int(0) == 42
  pub fn int(self, i: i64) -> i64 { self.get(i).to_i64() else 0 }
}

impl Run {
  /// The threads at whose position the characters of `s` come next, moved past them.
  /// ex: start("abc").text("ab").threads.map(.at) == [2]
  /// ex: start("abc").text("b").threads.is_empty()
  pub fn text(self, s: str) -> Run {
    let cs = s.chars()
    self.moved(
      self.threads.filter_map(
        |t| if follows(self.chars, t.at, cs) { Some(advanced(t, cs.len())) } else { None },
      ),
    )
  }

  /// The threads whose next character `keep` accepts, moved past it.
  /// ex: start("7a").class(|c| c >= "0" && c <= "9").threads.map(.at) == [1]
  pub fn class(self, keep: fn(str) -> bool) -> Run {
    let n = self.chars.len()
    self.moved(
      self.threads.filter_map(
        |t| if t.at < n && keep(self.chars[t.at]) { Some(advanced(t, 1)) } else { None },
      ),
    )
  }

  /// The threads that have a next character, moved past it: the pattern `.`.
  /// ex: start("").any().threads.is_empty()
  pub fn any(self) -> Run {
    let n = self.chars.len()
    self.moved(self.threads.filter_map(|t| if t.at < n { Some(advanced(t, 1)) } else { None }))
  }

  /// The threads at the start of the line: the pattern `^`.
  /// ex: start("a").bol().threads.len() == 1
  pub fn bol(self) -> Run { self.moved(self.threads.filter(|t| t.at == 0)) }

  /// The threads at the end of the line: the pattern `$`.
  /// ex: start("a").eol().threads.is_empty()
  pub fn eol(self) -> Run {
    let n = self.chars.len()
    self.moved(self.threads.filter(|t| t.at == n))
  }

  /// The steps one after another.
  /// ex: start("ab").seq([|r| r.text("a"), |r| r.text("b")]).threads.map(.at) == [2]
  pub fn seq(self, steps: List<fn(Run) -> Run>) -> Run {
    var out = self
    for step in steps { out = step(out) }
    out
  }

  /// Each thread through each branch, the first branch preferred.
  /// ex: start("ab").alt([|r| r.text("a"), |r| r.text("ab")]).threads.map(.at) == [1, 2]
  pub fn alt(self, branches: List<fn(Run) -> Run>) -> Run {
    var out: List<Thread> = []
    for t in self.threads { for b in branches { out.extend(b(self.only(t)).threads) } }
    self.moved(first_at_each(out))
  }

  /// Each thread through `body` as many times as it goes on, the most preferred: the pattern
  /// `x*`. A pass of `body` that moves no thread ends the repeating.
  /// ex: start("aab").star(|r| r.text("a")).threads.map(.at) == [2, 1, 0]
  pub fn star(self, body: fn(Run) -> Run) -> Run {
    var seen: List<bool> = List.repeat(false, self.chars.len() + 1)
    var out: List<Thread> = []
    for t in self.threads { self.repeat(t, body, inout seen, inout out) }
    self.moved(out)
  }

  /// `body` once, then as many times more as it goes on: the pattern `x+`.
  /// ex: start("aab").plus(|r| r.text("a")).threads.map(.at) == [2, 1]
  pub fn plus(self, body: fn(Run) -> Run) -> Run { body(self).star(body) }

  /// Each thread through `body`, or past it, through it preferred: the pattern `x?`.
  /// ex: start("ab").opt(|r| r.text("a")).threads.map(.at) == [1, 0]
  pub fn opt(self, body: fn(Run) -> Run) -> Run {
    var out: List<Thread> = []
    for t in self.threads {
      out.extend(body(self.only(t)).threads)
      out.push(t)
    }
    self.moved(first_at_each(out))
  }

  /// `body` as group `i`: each thread that comes out of it records where the group started
  /// and where it ends.
  /// ex: start("ab").group(0, |r| r.text("a")).threads.map(.caps) == [[0, 1]]
  pub fn group(self, i: i64, body: fn(Run) -> Run) -> Run {
    let opened = self.moved(self.threads.map(|t| marked(t, 2 * i)))
    self.moved(body(opened).threads.map(|t| marked(t, 2 * i + 1)))
  }

  // The run with other threads.
  fn moved(self, threads: List<Thread>) -> Run { Run { chars: self.chars, threads } }

  // The run of one thread.
  fn only(self, t: Thread) -> Run { Run { chars: self.chars, threads: [t] } }

  // The threads that repeating `body` gives from `t`, each after those that repeat further,
  // and none at a position that an earlier thread reached, which can give no match that the
  // earlier one doesn't.
  fn repeat(
    self,
    t: Thread,
    body: fn(Run) -> Run,
    inout seen: List<bool>,
    inout out: List<Thread>,
  ) {
    if seen[t.at] { return }
    seen[t.at] = true
    for u in body(self.only(t)).threads {
      if u.at > t.at { self.repeat(u, body, inout seen, inout out) }
    }
    out.push(t)
  }
}

// Whether the characters `cs` come at `at` in `chars`.
fn follows(chars: List<str>, at: i64, cs: List<str>) -> bool {
  if at + cs.len() > chars.len() { return false }
  var i = 0
  while i < cs.len() {
    if chars[at + i] != cs[i] { return false }
    i += 1
  }
  true
}

fn advanced(t: Thread, n: i64) -> Thread { Thread { ..t, at: t.at + n } }

// The first of the threads at each position, in their order.
fn first_at_each(ts: List<Thread>) -> List<Thread> {
  var seen: List<i64> = []
  var out: List<Thread> = []
  for t in ts {
    if !seen.contains(t.at) {
      seen.push(t.at)
      out.push(t)
    }
  }
  out
}

// The thread with its position recorded in the slot `slot` of its groups.
fn marked(t: Thread, slot: i64) -> Thread {
  var caps = t.caps
  caps[slot] = t.at
  Thread { ..t, caps }
}

/// The first match of `body` in `line`, from the leftmost position where one starts, or only
/// from its start when `anchored`, with `groups` groups besides the whole match.
/// ex: search("x12", 0, false, |r| r.plus(|r| r.class(|c| c >= "0" && c <= "9"))).map(|m| m.get(0)) == Some("12")
/// ex: search("x12", 0, true, |r| r.text("1")).is_none()
pub fn search(line: str, groups: i64, anchored: bool, body: fn(Run) -> Run) -> Option<Captures> {
  let chars = line.chars()
  let last = if anchored { 0 } else { chars.len() }
  for from in 0..last + 1 {
    let first = Thread { at: from, caps: List.repeat(-1, 2 * groups + 2) }
    if let Some(t) = body(Run { chars, threads: [first] }).threads.first() {
      var caps = t.caps
      caps[0] = from
      caps[1] = t.at
      return Some(Captures { groups: List.generate(groups + 1, |g| span(chars, caps, g)) })
    }
  }
  None
}

// The text of group `g`, whose start and end are in `caps`.
fn span(chars: List<str>, caps: List<i64>, g: i64) -> Option<str> {
  if caps[2 * g] < 0 || caps[2 * g + 1] < 0 { return None }
  Some("".join(chars.slice(caps[2 * g], caps[2 * g + 1])))
}

/// A run with one thread, at the start of `line`, which has no group.
/// ex: start("ab").threads.map(.at) == [0]
pub fn start(line: str) -> Run {
  Run { chars: line.chars(), threads: [Thread { at: 0, caps: [-1, -1] }] }
}
```

`rx.lt`:

```stilt fragment
// `regex!`, a procedural macro (macros.procedural-declarations) that reads a pattern while the
// program is checked and writes its matcher, a composition of the steps of `matcher`.
//
// The patterns: a character stands for itself; `.` for any character; `[…]` for one of the
// characters and ranges it lists, `[^…]` for any other, with `-` first or last standing for
// itself; `\d`, `\w` and `\s` for a digit, a word character and a space or tab, and `\D`, `\W`
// and `\S` for any other; `\` before any other character that is neither a letter nor a digit
// for that character; `(…)` for a group, numbered by its `(` from 1; `x*`, `x+` and `x?` for
// `x` repeated any number of times, at least once and at most once, as many times as it can;
// `a|b` for either, `a` preferred; and `^` and `$` for the start and the end of the line.

use std.meta
use matcher

// A pattern, read.
type Node =
  | Lit(str)
  | Any
  | Class(bool, List<(str, str)>)
  | Seq(List<Node>)
  | Alt(List<Node>)
  | Star(Node)
  | Plus(Node)
  | Opt(Node)
  | Group(i64, Node)
  | Bol
  | Eol

// A pattern being read: its characters, the byte where each starts in its text, which has one
// more for the end, the position of the next, and how many groups it has opened.
type Reader = { chars: List<str>, offsets: List<i64>, at: i64, groups: i64, text: meta.Text }

/// `regex!("^(\\d+) (GET|POST) (.*)$")`: a function that takes a line and gives the first match
/// of the pattern in it, with the text of each group, or `None`. A pattern that can't be read
/// is an error at its first character that can't stand where it is.
pub macro regex(pattern: meta.Text) -> meta.Expr / raise<meta.Error> {
  var r = try reader(pattern)
  let node = try alternation(inout r)
  if r.at < r.chars.len() { raise fail(r, r.at, "this `)` closes no `(`") }
  let anchored = match node {
    Seq(items) => items.first() == Some(Bol)
    _ => false
  }
  let body = code(node)
  let groups = r.groups
  quote { |line: str| matcher.search(line, $groups, $anchored, $body) }
}

// A reader at the start of the pattern's value.
fn reader(pattern: meta.Text) -> Reader / raise<meta.Error> {
  let chars = pattern.value().chars()
  var offsets: List<i64> = []
  var n = 0
  for c in chars {
    offsets.push(n)
    n += c.len()
  }
  offsets.push(n)
  Reader { chars, offsets, at: 0, groups: 0, text: pattern }
}

// The error at the character `at`, saying `message`.
fn fail(r: Reader, at: i64, message: str) -> meta.Error {
  meta.error(r.text.span(r.offsets[at], r.offsets[at + 1]), message)
}

// The next character, or "" at the end.
fn peek(r: Reader) -> str { r.chars.get(r.at) else "" }

// Branches separated by `|`.
fn alternation(inout r: Reader) -> Node / raise<meta.Error> {
  var branches = [try sequence(inout r)]
  while peek(r) == "|" {
    r.at += 1
    branches.push(try sequence(inout r))
  }
  if branches.len() == 1 { branches[0] } else { Alt(branches) }
}

// Items one after another, up to a `|`, a `)` or the end, the characters that follow one
// another joined into one literal.
fn sequence(inout r: Reader) -> Node / raise<meta.Error> {
  var items: List<Node> = []
  while r.at < r.chars.len() && peek(r) != "|" && peek(r) != ")" {
    let item = try repeated(inout r)
    match (items.last(), item) {
      (Some(Lit(a)), Lit(b)) => { items[items.len() - 1] = Lit("{a}{b}") }
      _ => items.push(item)
    }
  }
  Seq(items)
}

// An atom, and the `*`, `+` or `?` after it.
fn repeated(inout r: Reader) -> Node / raise<meta.Error> {
  let a = try atom(inout r)
  let wrap = match peek(r) {
    "*" => Star(a)
    "+" => Plus(a)
    "?" => Opt(a)
    _ => return a
  }
  r.at += 1
  wrap
}

fn atom(inout r: Reader) -> Node / raise<meta.Error> {
  let at = r.at
  let c = peek(r)
  r.at += 1
  match c {
    "(" => {
      r.groups += 1
      let i = r.groups
      let inner = try alternation(inout r)
      if peek(r) != ")" { raise fail(r, at, "this `(` is never closed") }
      r.at += 1
      Group(i, inner)
    }
    "[" => try class(inout r, at)
    "." => Any
    "^" => Bol
    "$" => Eol
    "*" | "+" | "?" => raise fail(r, at, "`{c}` follows nothing it could repeat")
    "\\" => try escape(inout r, at)
    _ => Lit(c)
  }
}

// What follows the `\` at `at`, outside a class.
fn escape(inout r: Reader, at: i64) -> Node / raise<meta.Error> {
  let c = peek(r)
  if c == "" { raise fail(r, at, "this `\\` escapes nothing") }
  r.at += 1
  match c {
    "d" => Class(false, DIGITS)
    "D" => Class(true, DIGITS)
    "w" => Class(false, WORD)
    "W" => Class(true, WORD)
    "s" => Class(false, SPACE)
    "S" => Class(true, SPACE)
    _ => if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
      raise fail(r, at, "`\\{c}` is no escape of a pattern")
    } else {
      Lit(c)
    }
  }
}

const DIGITS: List<(str, str)> = [("0", "9")]

const WORD: List<(str, str)> = [("a", "z"), ("A", "Z"), ("0", "9"), ("_", "_")]

const SPACE: List<(str, str)> = [(" ", " "), ("\t", "\t")]

// A class, after its `[` at `at`.
fn class(inout r: Reader, at: i64) -> Node / raise<meta.Error> {
  let negated = peek(r) == "^"
  if negated { r.at += 1 }
  var ranges: List<(str, str)> = []
  while peek(r) != "]" {
    if peek(r) == "" { raise fail(r, at, "this `[` is never closed") }
    ranges.extend(try member(inout r))
  }
  if ranges.is_empty() { raise fail(r, r.at, "a class lists at least one character") }
  r.at += 1
  Class(negated, ranges)
}

// One character of a class, a range or an escape.
fn member(inout r: Reader) -> List<(str, str)> / raise<meta.Error> {
  let lo = try one(inout r)
  if peek(r) != "-" || r.chars.get(r.at + 1) == Some("]") { return lo }
  let dash = r.at
  r.at += 1
  let hi = try one(inout r)
  match (lo, hi) {
    ([(a, a2)], [(b, b2)]) if a == a2 && b == b2 && a <= b => [(a, b)]
    _ => raise fail(r, dash, "this `-` joins no range")
  }
}

// A character of a class, or the characters of an escape.
fn one(inout r: Reader) -> List<(str, str)> / raise<meta.Error> {
  let at = r.at
  let c = peek(r)
  r.at += 1
  if c != "\\" { return [(c, c)] }
  let e = peek(r)
  r.at += 1
  match e {
    "d" => DIGITS
    "w" => WORD
    "s" => SPACE
    "" => raise fail(r, at, "this `\\` escapes nothing")
    _ => if e.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
      raise fail(r, at, "`\\{e}` is no escape of a class")
    } else {
      [(e, e)]
    }
  }
}

// The step of a node: a function from the threads before it to the threads after it.
fn code(n: Node) -> meta.Expr {
  match n {
    Lit(s) => quote { |r| r.text($s) }
    Any => quote { |r| r.any() }
    Class(negated, ranges) => {
      let c = meta.fresh("c")
      let accepted = accepts(c, ranges)
      if negated {
        quote { |r| r.class(|$c| !$accepted) }
      } else {
        quote { |r| r.class(|$c| $accepted) }
      }
    }
    Seq(items) => match items.len() {
      0 => quote { |r| r }
      1 => code(items[0])
      _ => {
        let steps = items.map(code)
        quote { |r| r.seq([$..steps]) }
      }
    }
    Alt(items) => {
      let branches = items.map(code)
      quote { |r| r.alt([$..branches]) }
    }
    Star(a) => {
      let body = code(a)
      quote { |r| r.star($body) }
    }
    Plus(a) => {
      let body = code(a)
      quote { |r| r.plus($body) }
    }
    Opt(a) => {
      let body = code(a)
      quote { |r| r.opt($body) }
    }
    Group(i, a) => {
      let body = code(a)
      quote { |r| r.group($i, $body) }
    }
    Bol => quote { |r| r.bol() }
    Eol => quote { |r| r.eol() }
  }
}

// Whether the character `c` is in one of the ranges.
fn accepts(c: meta.Name, ranges: List<(str, str)>) -> meta.Expr {
  var accepted = within(c, ranges[0])
  for range in ranges.skip(1) {
    let next = within(c, range)
    accepted = quote { $accepted || $next }
  }
  accepted
}

fn within(c: meta.Name, range: (str, str)) -> meta.Expr {
  let (lo, hi) = range
  if lo == hi { quote { $c == $lo } } else { quote { $c >= $lo && $c <= $hi } }
}
```
